route: mono — what monotone readouts can and cannot do: the negative side of the blow-up dichotomy, tested at the smallest open size
headline: Realisability of a prescribed improvement orientation by a stopping SSG with exactly m Max vertices is EQUIVALENT to a concave interpolation problem — one player buys affine readouts, the second buys concavity, and nothing else (thm:mono-iff) — and the negative half of rem:blowup-realise's dichotomy is FALSE as a structural theorem: all 18 AUSO classes of the 3-cube, including both non-Holt–Klee ones, are improvement orientations of explicit stopping SSGs (verified from the game), and a ONE-PLAYER game already presents, on one facet of a 4-dimensional Max cube, the single-coordinate translate of the 3-cube it presents on the parallel facet (13 exact witnesses, N = 55..145) — the same inner dimension and the same operation the second level of thm:blowup needs. What survives on the negative side is arithmetic, not structure: k >= log2 chi_HK(s) Min vertices (thm:mono-kbound), and 2^{Omega(m)} vertices for almost every AUSO (prop:mono-count).

results.name: lem:mono-readout (the readout theorem)
results.statement: Let G be a stopping SSG with Vmax = {x_1..x_m}. For y in [0,1]^m let G[y] be G with every Max vertex turned into a sink of payoff y_v, and F_{v,a}(y) := val_{G[y]}(v^{(a)}). Then (a) G[y] is stopping and F_{v,a}(y) = min over positional Min strategies tau of (q^{v,a,tau} + p^{v,a,tau}.y), the first-passage law from v^{(a)} onto Vmax and t1; every piece is SUBSTOCHASTIC (p >= 0, q >= 0, |p|_1 + q <= 1), so F_{v,a} is nondecreasing, CONCAVE and sup-norm 1-Lipschitz, and is a single affine map when Vmin is empty. (b) val_sigma|Vmax is the UNIQUE fixed point x_sigma of y_v = F_{v,sigma(v)}(y), and val_sigma = val_{G[x_sigma]} off Vmax. (c) v in S_sigma iff F_{v,1-sigma(v)}(x_sigma) > x_sigma(v); v is flat at sigma iff equality.
results.argument: A trap of G[y] involves no Max vertex and has the same successors as in G, so it is a trap of G, empty by lem:trapchar; G[y] is a one-player Min game, so by thm:lfp-general its value is the componentwise min over positional tau of an absorption expectation, affine in y with substochastic coefficients. For (b), val_sigma is a fixed point of the Shapley operator of G[x] and of T_sigma; both games are stopping so thm:contraction gives uniqueness in both directions. (c) is (b) read twice.
results.verification: t_sanity.py: recomputed val_sigma exactly for B1_game.json (58 vertices, one player), AP_m4_k0_den256_s200_game.json (100, one player) and ap_h7_game.json (G#, 4 Max, 2 Min); t_gsharp.py extracts G#'s eight readouts exactly from the game and recomputes its outmap from the readouts alone.

results.name: lem:mono-reduce (eliminating a vertex's own value)
results.statement: Every affine piece of F_{v,a} has self-coefficient p_v < 1, so t = F_{v,a}(y_{-v},t) has a unique solution Psi_{v,a}(y_{-v}); Psi_{v,a} : [0,1]^{m-1} -> [0,1] is again a minimum of finitely many substochastic affine maps (Psi = min_tau Psi^tau), x_sigma(v) = Psi_{v,sigma(v)}(x_{sigma,-v}), and v in S_sigma iff Psi_{v,1-sigma(v)}(x_{sigma,-v}) > Psi_{v,sigma(v)}(x_{sigma,-v}).
results.argument: p_v = 1 would mean the token returns from v to v with probability 1 under some positional pair, contradicting stopping. Solving t = q + p_{-v}.y + p_v t gives gradient p_{-v}/(1-p_v) >= 0 and intercept q/(1-p_v) >= 0 with (|p_{-v}|_1 + q)/(1-p_v) <= 1. Psi = min_tau Psi^tau because A_tau >= F gives Psi^tau >= Psi, and the tau attaining the min at t = Psi(y) has Psi^tau(y) = Psi(y).
results.verification: t_gsharp.py performs exactly this elimination on G# in exact rationals and checks the fixed-point identity and nondegeneracy at all 64 incidences.

results.name: thm:mono-iff (realisability = concave interpolation)
results.statement: (a) If s is the improvement outmap of a nondegenerate stopping SSG with |Vmax| = m and |Vmin| = k, then (Psi_{v,a}) is a readout system of order (m, 2^k) realising s, and of order (m,1) — all readouts affine — when Vmin is empty. (b) Conversely, a dyadic delta-leaky readout system of order (m,r) realising s yields a nondegenerate stopping SSG with exactly m Max vertices, at most 2m(r-1) Min vertices and average vertices only besides, whose improvement outmap is s.
results.argument: (a) is lem:mono-readout + lem:mono-reduce. (b) Build m Max vertices; for each (v,a) a list of r-1 Min vertices selecting among the r pieces; each piece is a Knuth–Yao DDG tree of fair coins for its dyadic law (the sec:fold binary-expansion chain, implemented here). Every gadget leaks >= delta to t0, so every positional pair's operator is a delta-contraction and the only trap is empty; the readouts are the prescribed Psi, so val_sigma|Vmax = x_sigma by lem:mono-reduce and the outmap is s.
results.verification: t_exact.py / t_verify3.py / t_vertrans.py build 34 explicit games this way and verify each FROM THE GAME: stopping by the trap characterisation (lem:trapchar), then T_sigma(cand) = cand at every vertex in exact rationals (a stopping game's operator has a unique fixed point, so this identifies val_sigma), then the outmap and nondegeneracy.

results.name: prop:mono-m3 (dimension three, settled)
results.statement: The 3-cube has 728 AUSOs in 18 classes, 16 Holt–Klee. (a) Each of the 16 Holt–Klee classes is the improvement orientation of a nondegenerate ONE-PLAYER stopping SSG, and by prop:oneplayer-lp the two others are not: at m = 3 one-player realisability is EXACTLY Holt–Klee. (b) All 18 classes — the two non-Holt–Klee ones included — are improvement orientations of nondegenerate stopping SSGs with three Max vertices, with at most two pieces per readout (six Min vertices); the games have 28 <= N <= 62 for the sixteen one-player ones and N = 98, N = 170 for the two others, denominators 64 to 512. The height-4 orientation B(1-cube) = (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2) is realised here on 39 vertices, against 58 in scripts/blowup/B1_game.json. (c) chi_HK = 1 on the sixteen Holt–Klee classes and 2 on the two others.
results.argument: Exhaustive enumeration of the 3-cube AUSOs and classes; readout systems found by successive linear programming and by a (1+lambda) evolution strategy in readout space; then thm:mono-iff(b) turns each into an explicit game.
results.verification: cubes.py (enumeration), t_all3b.py (search, all3b.log: 18/18, r=1 for exactly the 16 Holt–Klee classes), t_verify3.py (verify3.log: 18/18 verified exactly and from the game; all3_verified.json, game_m3_*.json), chk.py (chi_HK by BFS over the agreement masks of all 656 Holt–Klee AUSOs of the 3-cube).

results.name: prop:mono-translate (the translate operation is realised, already by one player)
results.statement: Say s carries a single-coordinate translate at inner dimension d if inside some (d+1)-face the two parallel d-faces are related by translation of the inner cube by a single coordinate e_j and are different. Of the 728 AUSOs of the 3-cube, 168 (four classes) carry a facet translate at inner dimension 2; all four are realised (prop:mono-m3) and two of them — (0,1,2,3,5,4,7,6) and (0,1,3,2,7,6,4,5) — by ONE-PLAYER games. At m = 4, 182 of the 12640 classes carry a facet translate, i.e. a translate of a 3-CUBE, which is the inner dimension B^2 needs; thirteen of them are improvement orientations of nondegenerate ONE-PLAYER stopping SSGs, with 55 <= N <= 145 (four Max, no Min) and denominators 64 to 1024, heights 2, 3 and 4 — e.g. the height-4 outmap (7,2,13,8,3,6,9,12,15,10,0,5,11,14,4,1) with translate pair (c,j) = (0,2), realised on 77 vertices at denominator 128.
results.argument: The translate property is invariant under the automorphism group (a pair (c,j) maps to (pi(c),pi(j)) and the condition is symmetric in the two faces), so it is tested on the class representatives. The realisations come from sampling affine readout systems at random — which samples exactly the one-player realisable orientations — followed by dyadic rounding and the exact verification of thm:mono-iff(b).
results.verification: t_translate.py (translate4_r1.log: 182/12640 classes; 13 realised at r = 1 in 250000 samples), t_vertrans.py (all 13 verified exactly and from the game; trans4_verified.json, trans4_*_game.json), t_subtrans.py (face scan of B^2 and of the height-7 orientation).

results.name: prop:mono-gsharp (G# as a readout system)
results.statement: G# of prop:auso-seven has eight readouts Psi_{v,a}, each a minimum of at most TWO distinct substochastic affine maps of the other three Max values (five of the eight are single affine maps), and the outmap recomputed from those eight functions alone is the height-7 orientation (0,1,3,6,7,4,13,10,14,15,9,12,11,8,5,2). So the height-7 orbit is realised by a readout system of order (4,2), and three Min vertices suffice for it in the construction of thm:mono-iff(b).
results.argument: Expand the average part (a DAG) to the harmonic normal form over the controlled vertices; eliminate the two Min vertices for each of the four tau to get affine maps over the four Max values; solve away each vertex's own value as in lem:mono-reduce; take the componentwise minimum over all 4^4 selections.
results.verification: t_gsharp.py, exact rationals; the fixed-point identity and nondegeneracy asserted at each of the 64 incidences; output gsharp_readouts.json.

results.name: prop:mono-hull (the convex-position condition)
results.statement: For a nondegenerate stopping SSG with |Vmax| = m and value configuration (x_sigma): for every sigma and every v NOT in s_G(sigma), x_sigma is not in the convex hull of {x_{sigma'} : sigma'(v) != sigma(v)}.
results.argument: h(y) := Psi_{v,1-sigma(v)}(y_{-v}) - y_v is concave, vanishes at every x_{sigma'} of the opposite v-face by lem:mono-reduce, and a concave function vanishing on a set is >= 0 on its convex hull; but h(x_sigma) < 0 exactly when v is not switchable.
results.verification: t_laws3.py: 708 incidences over 34 explicit games (the 18 of prop:mono-m3, the 13 of prop:mono-translate, B1_game, AP_m4, G#), none inside the opposite hull.

results.name: prop:mono-switchmax (no foreign strict maximiser)
results.statement: If u in S_sigma and d := val_{sigma[u]} - val_sigma restricted to Vmax (>= 0 by lem:switch), then d(v) <= max_{w != v} d(w) for every v != u; so if d has a unique maximising coordinate it is u. This is the two-player form of the one-player consequence of thm:impedance, and uses only monotonicity and |p|_1 <= 1.
results.argument: For v != u the two profiles agree at v, so d(v) = Psi_{v,a}(x_{sigma',-v}) - Psi_{v,a}(x_{sigma,-v}) with x_{sigma',-v} >= x_{sigma,-v}; a concave function with supergradients in {p >= 0, |p|_1 <= 1} increases by at most the largest coordinate increase.
results.verification: t_laws3.py: 708 improving switches over the same 34 games, every one with a unique maximiser and always at the switched vertex.

results.name: thm:mono-kbound (a lower bound on the number of Min vertices)
results.statement: Let chi_HK(s) be the least R for which s is a pointwise selection from R Holt–Klee AUSOs of the m-cube. For a nondegenerate stopping SSG with m Max and k Min vertices, chi_HK(s_G) <= 2^k, so k >= log2 chi_HK(s_G); chi_HK does not increase under passing to a face, so every face gives such a bound. In particular a non-Holt–Klee s needs k >= 1, and if one Min strategy is a best response to every sigma then s is Holt–Klee.
results.argument: Pick a Min best response tau_sigma for each sigma; on S_tau = {sigma : tau_sigma = tau} the one-player game G_tau (Min frozen) has the same value vectors as G, hence the same outmap and no flat coordinate there. lem:mono-perturb (proved here: perturbing the intercepts of the affine readouts by a generic dyadic eta, after shrinking the rows, makes G_tau nondegenerate while preserving the strict comparisons on S_tau, because dD_{sigma,v}/d eta_{v,1-sigma(v)} = 1 identically, so each zero set is closed with empty interior) makes it nondegenerate, and prop:oneplayer-lp makes its orientation Holt–Klee.
results.verification: chk.py and bigagree.py compute chi_HK exactly: at m = 3 it is 1 on the sixteen Holt–Klee classes and 2 on the two others; the height-7 orientation at m = 4 has chi_HK = 2 (so the bound gives only k >= 1 where G# uses k = 2); of B^2's forty 3-faces, 34 have chi_HK = 1 and 6 have 2, and each of its ten 4-faces has chi_HK <= 2, so all the bound yields for B^2 is k >= 1.

results.name: prop:mono-proj (sink projection, in general)
results.statement: For a stopping SSG with m Max and k Min vertices in which no profile ties a controlled vertex, the profile orientation of the (m+k)-cube (a controlled vertex is out when its owner strictly prefers its other action under val_{sigma,tau}) is a unique sink orientation; the sink of {sigma} x {0,1}^k is (sigma, tau_sigma) with tau_sigma Min's best response, and the Max coordinates out there are exactly S_sigma. So every improvement orientation of a nondegenerate stopping SSG is the sink projection of a USO of the (m+k)-cube.
results.argument: On any face, freezing the other controlled vertices gives a stopping subgame G_F; a profile is a sink of the face iff T_{G_F} fixes val_{sigma,tau}, iff val_{sigma,tau} = val_{G_F}, which happens for at least one profile and, without ties, exactly one. On the Min face of sigma, G_F is G with Max frozen and val_{G_F} = val_sigma.
results.verification: generalises prop:gsharp-bigcube's computed observation; no new computation needed. Acyclicity and Holt–Klee of the big cube are NOT claimed in general.

results.name: prop:mono-count (counting in readout space)
results.statement: At most 2^{O(r m^3 log 2r)} outmaps of the m-cube are realised by readout systems of order (m,r), while the number of AUSOs of the m-cube is at least 728^{2^{m-3}} > 2^{1.18 * 2^m}. Hence all but a 2^{-Omega(2^m)} fraction of AUSOs need more than c 2^m/m^4 pieces in some readout, hence more than m - 4 log2 m - O(1) Min vertices and 2^{Omega(m)} vertices, in any realisation.
results.argument: A readout system of order (m,r) is a point of R^{2rm^2}; x_sigma for each piece-selection is a ratio of m x m determinants, so the outmap is determined by the sign vector of at most r^m m 2^m polynomials of degree O(m), and Warren's bound gives (4eDM/n)^n. For the lower bound, combing one coordinate over two arbitrary facet AUSOs is again an AUSO, so A(m) >= A(m-1)^2 with A(3) = 728.
results.verification: A(3) = 728 is the exhaustive count in cubes.py; the rest is the argument of prop:auso-size transferred to the readout parametrisation and is labelled as such.

results.name: Coverage measurement at m = 4
results.statement: Random readout systems, whose hits are realisations: with affine readouts (r = 1), 150000 samples hit 541 of the 12640 AUSO classes of the 4-cube and EVERY hit is Holt–Klee (0 of the 6527 non-Holt–Klee classes), as prop:oneplayer-lp requires; by height, 1/1, 215/423 (h=2 HK), 298/2503 (h=3 HK), 27/2401 (h=4 HK), 0 above. With r = 2 (one Min vertex per readout), another 150000 samples hit 434 classes of which 44 are NOT Holt–Klee: 32 of the 331 non-Holt–Klee classes of height 2 and 12 of the 2273 of height 3.
results.argument: Sampling in readout space samples exactly the realisable orientations, so each hit is a realisation with the stated number of Min vertices; misses are not evidence, and sampling visibly reaches only low heights.
results.verification: t_cover4b.py, logs cover4b_r1.log and cover4b_r2.log, census /tmp/.../solo/census/classes4.txt (12640 classes, orbit table of 4792176 entries).

results.name: B^2 at m = 5 (the smallest open instance): not settled, and the search is not evidence
results.statement: B^2 = (7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6,24,9,27,14,31,28,29,10,16,25,19,30,23,20,21,26,8,17,11,22,15,12,13,18), height 10, not Holt–Klee, 7 of its 10 four-faces and 6 of its 40 three-faces not Holt–Klee, three single-coordinate translates at inner dimension 3 (its own, between layers (0,0) and (1,0)). Successive linear programming in readout space, with a trust region and restarts, reached at best 126 of its 160 incidences (r = 2,3,4). The SAME method reached at best 52 of the 64 incidences of the height-7 orientation at m = 4 in 38 restarts with r = 2, 32 with r = 3 and 22 with r = 4 — and prop:mono-gsharp shows that orientation IS realised with r = 2. So the failure on B^2 carries no information.
results.argument: Calibration on a known-realisable target shows the search space is right and the search is weak.
results.verification: slp.py, t_slp.py, logs slp_B2_r*.log and slp_G7_r*.log; hunt.py, mono2.py and t_loop3.py record two further, weaker search methods with the same outcome.

gap: GAP: it is not known whether every acyclic unique sink orientation of the m-cube is realised by some readout system of finite order — equivalently, by some stopping SSG with exactly m Max vertices — and in particular whether the 5-cube orientation B^2 of thm:blowup is realised by a readout system of order (5,r) for small r.
next_steps:
1. The decisive computation is now cheap to state: for a FIXED value configuration x = (x_sigma) the existence of the readouts is a linear programme (rem:mono-iff, implemented in mono.py: concave_lp), so realisability of B^2 is "does there exist x in ([0,1]^5)^32 making ten small LPs feasible". Our bilinear alternations (mono2.py) and successive linear programming (slp.py) both fail on a target we know to be realisable, so the next step is a better outer search over x — a derivative-free optimiser on the 160-dimensional x with the softened LP margin as objective, or a homotopy from a realised neighbour of B^2 (e.g. one of the 13 verified m = 4 translate witnesses, extended by two outer coordinates).
2. thm:mono-kbound is the only instance-specific size bound we have and it is weak (k >= 1 everywhere we can compute it). Sharpening it needs chi_HK on 5-cube orientations, which needs the Holt–Klee AUSOs of the 5-cube; the branch-and-bound of bigagree.py (enumerate AUSOs agreeing with the target on at least half the vertices, then look for a Holt–Klee completion of the complement) is the right tool and scales to m = 5 only if the "agree on >= 16 of 32" bound prunes as hard there as it does at m = 4.
3. A construction theorem would settle the question outright: prove or refute "every AUSO of the m-cube is realised by a readout system of order (m, 2^{O(m)})". Our data (18/18 at m = 3 with r <= 2; 44 non-Holt–Klee classes at m = 4 with r = 2; G# with r = 2) is consistent with r = 2 always sufficing, which would be the sharpest possible positive statement and would make the pivot purely a question of the SIZE of the average part.
4. Still running when this report was written, and killed with the session: t_translate.py 4 250000 21 2 (log translate4_r2.log) — the r = 2 version of the m = 4 translate-class coverage. Its r = 1 half is complete and reported.

% ROUTE mono: what monotone readouts can and cannot do.
% Paste-ready for frontier.tex (amsthm style, \Cref references).
% Full file also at <code_dir>/mono.tex

\section{Monotone readouts: what a game can present on a face}\label{sec:mono}

\Cref{rem:blowup-realise} poses a dichotomy: either a gadget realises the
height-doubling blow-up of \Cref{thm:blowup}, or improvement orientations of
stopping SSGs cannot present, on one face of the Max cube, the translate of
what they present on a parallel face. This section settles the shape of the
question. It replaces the informal notion of a ``readout'' by an exact one,
proves that realisability by a stopping SSG with a prescribed number of Max
vertices is \emph{equivalent} to a concave interpolation problem, and uses that
equivalence to decide the question completely for $m\le3$: every acyclic unique
sink orientation of the $3$-cube --- including both orientations that violate
Holt--Klee --- is the improvement orientation of a stopping SSG. So no theorem
of the negative kind can be proved by structure alone; what is left is a
question about \emph{size}, and \Cref{thm:mono-kbound} is a lower bound of that
kind.

\subsection{The readout of a Max vertex}

\begin{definition}[Pinning, and the readouts]\label{def:mono-readout}
Let $G$ be a stopping SSG with $\Vmax=\{x_1,\dots,x_m\}$ and let
$y\in[0,1]^{m}$. Write $G[y]$ for the SSG obtained from $G$ by deleting the
outgoing edges of every Max vertex and declaring $x_v$ a sink of payoff $y_v$;
$G[y]$ has no Max vertices. For a Max vertex $v$ and an action $a\in\{0,1\}$
let $v^{(a)}$ be the corresponding successor and put
\[
  F_{v,a}(y)\;:=\;\val_{G[y]}\bigl(v^{(a)}\bigr).
\]
Call $(F_{v,a})_{v\le m,\,a\in\{0,1\}}$ the \emph{readouts} of $G$.
\end{definition}

Write $\Delta:=\{p\in\mathbb R^{m}_{\ge0}:|p|_1\le1\}$ and call an affine map
$y\mapsto q+p\cdot y$ \emph{substochastic} when $p\ge0$, $q\ge0$ and
$|p|_1+q\le1$: these are exactly the maps $y\mapsto\mathbb E[\text{payoff}]$ of
a first-passage law that lands on the $x_w$ with probabilities $p_w$, on $t_1$
with probability $q$ and on $t_0$ with the rest.

\begin{lemma}[The readout theorem]\label{lem:mono-readout}
Let $G$ be stopping with $|\Vmax|=m$. Then
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $G[y]$ is stopping for every $y$, and
      $F_{v,a}(y)=\min_{\tau}\bigl(q^{v,a,\tau}+p^{v,a,\tau}\cdot y\bigr)$,
      the minimum over the positional Min strategies of $G$, where
      $(p^{v,a,\tau},q^{v,a,\tau})$ is the first-passage law from $v^{(a)}$
      onto $\Vmax$ and onto $t_1$ when Min plays $\tau$. Each such affine map
      is substochastic. Hence every $F_{v,a}$ is nondecreasing, \emph{concave},
      and $1$-Lipschitz for the sup norm; and if $\Vmin=\emptyset$ it is a
      single substochastic affine map.
\item For every Max strategy $\sigma$ the vector
      $x_\sigma:=\val_\sigma|_{\Vmax}$ is the \emph{unique} $y\in[0,1]^m$ with
      $y_v=F_{v,\sigma(v)}(y)$ for all $v$, and $\val_\sigma=\val_{G[x_\sigma]}$
      off $\Vmax$.
\item $v\in S_\sigma$ iff $F_{v,1-\sigma(v)}(x_\sigma)>x_\sigma(v)$, and $v$ is
      flat at $\sigma$ (\Cref{def:flat}) iff equality holds.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) A trap of $G[y]$ is a set $U$ of vertices of $G[y]$ that are not sinks of
$G[y]$, so $U\cap\Vmax=\emptyset$, in which every average vertex has both
successors in $U$ and every controlled vertex some; the successors of the
vertices of $U$ are the same in $G$ and in $G[y]$, so $U$ is a trap of $G$ and
\Cref{lem:trapchar} makes it empty. $G[y]$ has only Min and average vertices,
so by \Cref{thm:lfp-general} its value is the componentwise minimum over the
positional $\tau$ of the value of the Markov chain obtained by freezing $\tau$;
that chain absorbs almost surely in $\Vmax\cup\{t_0,t_1\}$ because $G[y]$ is
stopping, and its value at $v^{(a)}$ is $\sum_w p^{v,a,\tau}_wy_w+q^{v,a,\tau}$
with $p,q\ge0$ and $|p|_1+q\le1$. A minimum of finitely many nondecreasing
affine maps is nondecreasing and concave, and $|p|_1\le1$ makes each piece
$1$-Lipschitz for $|\cdot|_\infty$.

(b) Put $x:=\val_\sigma|_{\Vmax}$. The Shapley operator of $G[x]$ and the
operator $T_\sigma$ of $G$ with Max frozen agree away from $\Vmax$, and at a
Max vertex the former pins the value to $x_v$ while the latter returns
$\val_\sigma(\sigma(v))$; since $\val_\sigma(\sigma(v))=\val_\sigma(v)=x_v$,
the vector $\val_\sigma$ is a fixed point of both. $G[x]$ is stopping, so by
\Cref{thm:contraction} its operator has a unique fixed point, whence
$\val_{G[x]}=\val_\sigma$ and
$F_{v,\sigma(v)}(x)=\val_\sigma(v^{(\sigma(v))})=x_v$. Conversely let $y$
satisfy $y_v=F_{v,\sigma(v)}(y)$ for all $v$. Then $\val_{G[y]}$ is a fixed
point of $T_\sigma$: away from $\Vmax$ the two operators agree, and at $x_v$
one has $T_\sigma(\val_{G[y]})(x_v)=\val_{G[y]}(v^{(\sigma(v))})=F_{v,\sigma(v)}(y)=y_v=\val_{G[y]}(x_v)$.
$G_\sigma$ is stopping, so $\val_{G[y]}=\val_\sigma$ and $y=x$.

(c) By (b), $\val_\sigma$ and $\val_{G[x_\sigma]}$ agree off $\Vmax$, so
$\val_\sigma(v^{(b)})=F_{v,b}(x_\sigma)$ for both $b$, and
$F_{v,\sigma(v)}(x_\sigma)=x_\sigma(v)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Eliminating a vertex's own value]\label{lem:mono-reduce}
In the situation of \Cref{lem:mono-readout} every affine piece of $F_{v,a}$ has
coefficient $p_v<1$, so for each $y_{-v}\in[0,1]^{m-1}$ the equation
$t=F_{v,a}(y_{-v},t)$ has a unique solution $\Psi_{v,a}(y_{-v})$. The function
$\Psi_{v,a}:[0,1]^{m-1}\to[0,1]$ is again a minimum of finitely many
substochastic affine maps --- namely $\Psi_{v,a}=\min_\tau\Psi^{\tau}_{v,a}$,
where $\Psi^\tau_{v,a}$ solves $t=q^{v,a,\tau}+p^{v,a,\tau}\cdot(y_{-v},t)$ ---
and
\[
  x_\sigma(v)=\Psi_{v,\sigma(v)}\bigl(x_{\sigma,-v}\bigr),
  \qquad
  v\in S_\sigma\iff
  \Psi_{v,1-\sigma(v)}\bigl(x_{\sigma,-v}\bigr)>\Psi_{v,\sigma(v)}\bigl(x_{\sigma,-v}\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If some piece had $p_v=1$ then under the pair $(\sigma,\tau)$ with
$\sigma(v)=a$ the token started at $v$ would return to $v$ with probability
one, never reaching a sink, contradicting stopping. So $t\mapsto
F_{v,a}(y_{-v},t)-t$ is strictly decreasing and has a unique zero. Writing
$p=(p_{-v},p_v)$, the solution of $t=q+p_{-v}\cdot y_{-v}+p_vt$ is
$(q+p_{-v}\cdot y_{-v})/(1-p_v)$, whose gradient and intercept are nonnegative
and satisfy $\bigl(|p_{-v}|_1+q\bigr)/(1-p_v)\le(1-p_v)/(1-p_v)=1$: again a
substochastic affine map, now in $m-1$ variables. For the minimum, $A_\tau\ge
F_{v,a}$ gives $\Psi^\tau\ge\Psi$, while the $\tau$ attaining the minimum at
$t=\Psi(y_{-v})$ has $\Psi^\tau(y_{-v})=\Psi(y_{-v})$. The two displayed
identities are \Cref{lem:mono-readout}(b),(c) read at $t=x_\sigma(v)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Readout system]\label{def:mono-system}
A \emph{readout system} of order $(m,r)$ is a family
$\Psi_{v,a}:[0,1]^{m-1}\to[0,1]$, $v\le m$, $a\in\{0,1\}$, each a minimum of at
most $r$ substochastic affine maps. It is \emph{$\delta$-leaky} if every piece
satisfies $|p|_1+q\le1-\delta$, and \emph{dyadic} if all coefficients are.
For $\sigma\in\{0,1\}^m$ let $x_\sigma$ be a fixed point of
$y\mapsto(\Psi_{v,\sigma(v)}(y_{-v}))_v$ (unique when $\delta>0$). The system
\emph{realises} an outmap $s$ if for every $\sigma$ and $v$
\[
  \Psi_{v,1-\sigma(v)}(x_{\sigma,-v})\ne x_\sigma(v),
  \quad\text{with}\quad
  \Psi_{v,1-\sigma(v)}(x_{\sigma,-v})> x_\sigma(v)\iff v\in s(\sigma).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Realisability is a concave interpolation problem]\label{thm:mono-iff}
Let $s:\{0,1\}^m\to2^{[m]}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item If $s$ is the improvement outmap of a nondegenerate stopping SSG $G$
      with $|\Vmax|=m$ and $|\Vmin|=k$, then the family $(\Psi_{v,a})$ of
      \Cref{lem:mono-reduce} is a readout system of order $(m,2^{k})$ realising
      $s$; with $\Vmin=\emptyset$ it has $r=1$, i.e.\ all readouts are affine.
\item Conversely, if a dyadic $\delta$-leaky readout system of order $(m,r)$
      with $\delta>0$ realises $s$, then $s$ is the improvement outmap of a
      nondegenerate stopping SSG with exactly $m$ Max vertices, at most
      $2m(r-1)$ Min vertices, and average vertices only besides.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(a) is \Cref{lem:mono-readout} and \Cref{lem:mono-reduce}; the number of pieces
is the number of positional Min strategies.

(b) Take $m$ Max vertices $x_1,\dots,x_m$. For each pair $(v,a)$ build a list
of $r-1$ Min vertices $u^{v,a}_1,\dots,u^{v,a}_{r-1}$, letting action $0$ of
$u^{v,a}_j$ enter the gadget of the $j$-th affine piece and action $1$ enter
$u^{v,a}_{j+1}$ (and, at $j=r-1$, the gadget of the $r$-th piece); the action
$a$ of $x_v$ points at $u^{v,a}_1$. Each piece $q+p\cdot y$ is realised by a
Knuth--Yao discrete distribution generating tree of fair coins for the dyadic
law that puts $p_w$ on $x_w$, $q$ on $t_1$ and $1-|p|_1-q\ge\delta$ on $t_0$;
this is the binary-expansion chain of \Cref{sec:fold}, and we implement and
verify it (\texttt{build.py}, \texttt{t\_exact.py}). The resulting game is
stopping: every gadget sends at least $\delta$ of its mass to $t_0$, so the
operator of any positional pair is a $\delta$-contraction and the only trap is
empty. Its readouts are the given $\Psi_{v,a}$ by construction, so by
\Cref{lem:mono-reduce} $\val_\sigma|_{\Vmax}=x_\sigma$ and the improvement
outmap is $s$; nondegeneracy is the strict inequality in
\Cref{def:mono-system}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:mono-iff}
\Cref{thm:mono-iff} turns realisability into a finite-dimensional geometric
question and separates the two players cleanly: \emph{one player buys affine
readouts, the second buys concavity, and nothing else}. Two consequences are
worth stating. First, for a fixed configuration $x=(x_\sigma)$ the existence of
the readouts is a \emph{linear programme}: a concave function interpolating
finite data exists iff each datum carries a supporting affine map dominating
the others, so the unknowns are, per pair $(v,a)$, the values $g_\sigma$ (free
where $\sigma(v)\ne a$, pinned to $x_\sigma(v)$ where $\sigma(v)=a$) and one
gradient $p_\sigma\in\Delta$ per point, with
$g_\sigma+p_\sigma\cdot(y_{\sigma'}-y_\sigma)\ge g_{\sigma'}$,
$q_\sigma:=g_\sigma-p_\sigma\cdot y_\sigma\ge0$ and $|p_\sigma|_1+q_\sigma\le
1-\delta$; the one-player case is the same programme with all $p_\sigma$ tied.
Second, \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} is exactly the statement that the affine
version of this programme forces Holt--Klee.
\end{remark}

\subsection{What concavity forbids}

\begin{proposition}[The convex-position condition]\label{prop:mono-hull}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping SSG with $|\Vmax|=m$ and let
$(x_\sigma)_{\sigma\in\{0,1\}^m}$ be its value configuration. Then for every
$\sigma$ and every $v\notin s_G(\sigma)$,
\[
  x_\sigma\;\notin\;\operatorname{conv}\bigl\{x_{\sigma'}\ :\
      \sigma'(v)\ne\sigma(v)\bigr\}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put $a:=1-\sigma(v)$ and $h(y):=\Psi_{v,a}(y_{-v})-y_v$ on $\mathbb R^m$, a
concave function (concave in $y_{-v}$, affine in $y_v$). For every $\sigma'$
with $\sigma'(v)=a$ we have $\Psi_{v,a}(x_{\sigma',-v})=x_{\sigma'}(v)$ by
\Cref{lem:mono-reduce}, so $h$ vanishes on the whole opposite $v$-face of the
configuration; a concave function vanishing on a set is nonnegative on its
convex hull. But $v\notin s_G(\sigma)$ gives $h(x_\sigma)<0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[No foreign strict maximiser]\label{prop:mono-switchmax}
Let $G$ be stopping, $u\in S_\sigma$ and $\sigma'=\sigma[u]$, and put
$d:=x_{\sigma'}-x_\sigma\ (\ge0$ by \Cref{lem:switch}$)$. Then
$d(v)\le\max_{w\ne v}d(w)$ for every $v\ne u$. Consequently, if $d$ has a
unique maximising coordinate then that coordinate is $u$: the value increase
caused by switching $u$ is nowhere strictly larger than at $u$ itself.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $v\ne u$ we have $\sigma(v)=\sigma'(v)=:a$, so
$d(v)=\Psi_{v,a}(x_{\sigma',-v})-\Psi_{v,a}(x_{\sigma,-v})$, and the two
arguments satisfy $x_{\sigma',-v}\ge x_{\sigma,-v}$. A concave function whose
supergradients lie in $\Delta$ satisfies, for $y'\ge y$,
$\Psi(y')-\Psi(y)\le g\cdot(y'-y)\le\max_w(y'-y)_w$ for a supergradient $g$ at
$y$, because $g\ge0$ and $|g|_1\le1$. If the maximum of $d$ were attained at a
single $v\ne u$ we would get $d(v)\le\max_{w\ne v}d(w)<d(v)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:mono-switchmax}
\Cref{prop:mono-switchmax} is the two-player form of the one-player consequence
of \Cref{thm:impedance}, where the increase at $w$ is the increase at $u$ times
a transfer impedance $h(w\!\to\!u)\le1$. The proof here uses nothing but
monotonicity and $|p|_1\le1$, so it holds with Min vertices present.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:mono-laws-measured}
Both laws were checked in exact arithmetic on $34$ explicit games: the
one-player $B(\text{1-cube})$ game on $58$ vertices, the one-player
$B(\text{2-cube})$ game on $100$, the two-player $G^{\sharp}$, the eighteen
games of \Cref{prop:mono-m3} and the thirteen of \Cref{prop:mono-translate}.
On all $708$ improving switches the increase $\val_{\sigma[u]}-\val_\sigma$ has
a \emph{unique} maximising coordinate and it is $u$ every time; and at all
$708$ incidences $(\sigma,v)$ with $v\notin s(\sigma)$ the vector $x_\sigma$
lies outside the convex hull of the opposite $v$-face, as
\Cref{prop:mono-hull} requires.
\end{remark}

\subsection{A lower bound on the number of Min vertices}

\begin{lemma}[Nondegenerate perturbation]\label{lem:mono-perturb}
Let $H$ be a one-player stopping SSG with $\Vmax$ of size $m$, and let
$\Sigma_0$ be a set of Max strategies at which $H$ has no flat coordinate.
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a nondegenerate one-player stopping SSG
$H'$ with the same $\Vmax$ whose improvement outmap agrees with $H$'s at every
$\sigma\in\Sigma_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:mono-reduce} with $\Vmin=\emptyset$, $H$ is given by $2m$ affine
readouts $\Psi_{v,a}(y)=q_{v,a}+p_{v,a}\cdot y$. Multiply every row by
$1-\varepsilon''$: the values move continuously, so for $\varepsilon''$ small
the finitely many strict inequalities that hold at the $\sigma\in\Sigma_0$
survive, and now every row has $|p|_1+q\le1-\varepsilon''$. Then perturb the
intercepts, $q_{v,a}\mapsto q_{v,a}+\eta_{v,a}$, with
$\eta\in(0,\varepsilon')^{2m}$ and $\varepsilon'<\varepsilon''$; the rows stay
substochastic and the game stopping. For
fixed $\sigma$ the fixed point $x_\sigma(\eta)$ depends only on the rows
$(v,\sigma(v))$, hence not on $\eta_{v,1-\sigma(v)}$; consequently
\[
  D_{\sigma,v}(\eta):=\Psi_{v,1-\sigma(v)}\bigl(x_\sigma(\eta)_{-v}\bigr)-x_\sigma(v)(\eta)
  \qquad\text{has}\qquad
  \partial D_{\sigma,v}/\partial\eta_{v,1-\sigma(v)}\equiv1 .
\]
So $D_{\sigma,v}$ is a rational function of $\eta$ that is nonconstant along
one coordinate direction at \emph{every} point; its zero set is closed with
empty interior. The union of the $m2^{m}$ zero sets is therefore closed and
nowhere dense, and its complement is open and dense, hence contains dyadic
rational points. Intersecting with a small enough ball about $\eta=0$
preserves substochasticity, stopping, and the finitely many strict
inequalities that hold at the $\sigma\in\Sigma_0$; picking a dyadic $\eta$
there and applying \Cref{thm:mono-iff}(b) produces $H'$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Holt--Klee selection number]\label{def:mono-chi}
For an outmap $s$ of the $m$-cube let $\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}(s)$ be the least $R$
for which there are Holt--Klee AUSOs $t_1,\dots,t_R$ of the $m$-cube with
$s(\sigma)\in\{t_1(\sigma),\dots,t_R(\sigma)\}$ for every $\sigma$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Min vertices are needed in proportion to the Holt--Klee defect]\label{thm:mono-kbound}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping SSG with $m$ Max and $k$ Min vertices and
improvement outmap $s$. Then $\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}(s)\le2^{k}$, so
\[
  k\;\ge\;\log_2\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}(s).
\]
Moreover $\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}$ does not increase under passing to a face, so
every face of $s$ gives such a bound. In particular a $\sigma\mapsto s(\sigma)$
that is not Holt--Klee needs $k\ge1$; and if $G$ has a single Min strategy that
is a best response to every $\sigma$, then $s$ is Holt--Klee.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For each $\sigma$ pick a Min best response $\tau_\sigma$ and let $T$ be the set
of chosen responses, $|T|\le2^k$. Fix $\tau\in T$ and let $G_\tau$ be $G$ with
Min frozen to $\tau$: a one-player stopping SSG (\Cref{lem:subgame}) with
$\val^{G_\tau}_\sigma\ge\val^{G}_\sigma$, with equality exactly when $\tau$ is
a best response to $\sigma$. Hence for every $\sigma$ in
$S_\tau:=\{\sigma:\tau_\sigma=\tau\}$ the two games have the same value vector
at $\sigma$, so the improvement outmap of $G_\tau$ at $\sigma$ equals
$s(\sigma)$, and $G_\tau$ has no flat coordinate there. By
\Cref{lem:mono-perturb} there is a \emph{nondegenerate} one-player stopping
$G'_\tau$ agreeing with $G_\tau$ at every $\sigma\in S_\tau$, and by
\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} its improvement orientation $t_\tau$ is Holt--Klee.
The family $(t_\tau)_{\tau\in T}$ is a Holt--Klee selection for $s$.
For faces: freezing a set of Max coordinates turns $G$ into a stopping SSG
with fewer Max vertices whose improvement outmap is the corresponding face of
$s$ (\Cref{lem:subgame}, \Cref{thm:opt-subcube}), and a face of a Holt--Klee
orientation is Holt--Klee. The last sentences are $R=1$ and $R\ge2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Sink projection, in general]\label{prop:mono-proj}
Let $G$ be stopping with $m$ Max and $k$ Min vertices and suppose no profile
$(\sigma,\tau)$ ties any controlled vertex's two successors. Orient the
$(m+k)$-cube of profiles by declaring a controlled vertex \emph{out} at
$(\sigma,\tau)$ when its owner strictly prefers its other action under
$\val_{\sigma,\tau}$. Then this orientation is a unique sink orientation;
for each $\sigma$ the sink of the face $\{\sigma\}\times\{0,1\}^k$ is
$(\sigma,\tau_\sigma)$ with $\tau_\sigma$ Min's best response to $\sigma$, and
the Max coordinates out there are exactly $S_\sigma$. So $s_G$ is the sink
projection of a unique sink orientation of the $(m+k)$-cube.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $F$ be a face: freeze the controlled vertices outside a set $C'$ at their
$F$-values, obtaining a stopping SSG $G_F$ (\Cref{lem:subgame}) whose
controlled vertices are $C'$. A profile of $F$ is a sink of $F$ iff no vertex
of $C'$ strictly prefers its other action under $\val_{\sigma,\tau}$, i.e.\ iff
$T_{G_F}(\val_{\sigma,\tau})=\val_{\sigma,\tau}$; $G_F$ is stopping, so by
\Cref{thm:contraction} this holds iff $\val_{\sigma,\tau}=\val_{G_F}$, which
happens for at least one profile (an optimal one) and, by the absence of ties,
for exactly one. For $F=\{\sigma\}\times\{0,1\}^k$ the game $G_F$ is $G$ with
Max frozen to $\sigma$, $\val_{G_F}=\val_\sigma$, and the sink is the profile
where $\tau$ is greedy for $\val_\sigma$; there Max's vertex $v$ is out iff
$\val_\sigma(v^{(1-\sigma(v))})>\val_\sigma(v^{(\sigma(v))})$, i.e.\ iff
$v\in S_\sigma$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:mono-proj}
\Cref{prop:mono-proj} makes the observation of \Cref{prop:gsharp-bigcube}
general: every improvement orientation of a nondegenerate stopping SSG is the
sink projection of a unique sink orientation of the $(m+k)$-cube. We do not
claim that orientation is acyclic or Holt--Klee in general; $G^{\sharp}$'s is
both, verified there. \Cref{thm:mono-kbound} is what the projection buys
quantitatively, and it is proved without any hypothesis on the big cube.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Dimension three is settled: no obstruction at all}

\begin{proposition}[$m=3$]\label{prop:mono-m3}
The $3$-cube has $728$ acyclic unique sink orientations in $18$ classes under
coordinate permutation and translation, $16$ of them Holt--Klee.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item Each of the $16$ Holt--Klee classes is the improvement orientation of a
      nondegenerate \emph{one-player} stopping SSG, and by
      \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} the two others are not. So at $m=3$ one-player
      realisability is \emph{exactly} the Holt--Klee condition.
\item Each of the $18$ classes --- the two non-Holt--Klee ones included --- is
      the improvement orientation of a nondegenerate stopping SSG with three
      Max vertices; readout systems with at most two pieces per readout
      suffice, so at most six Min vertices are needed. The explicit games have
      $28\le N\le62$ vertices for the sixteen one-player ones and $N=98$,
      $N=170$ for the two others (three Max, six Min, the rest average),
      denominators $64$ to $512$. In particular the height-$4$ orientation
      $B(\text{1-cube})=(0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2)$ of \Cref{rem:blowup-measured} is
      realised here on $39$ vertices rather than $58$.
\item $\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}=1$ on the sixteen Holt--Klee classes and $2$ on the
      two others, so \Cref{thm:mono-kbound} gives $k\ge1$ there and this is
      attained.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A computation. The $728$ orientations and the $18$ classes come from a
backtracking enumeration with the Szab\'o--Welzl condition and a depth-first
acyclicity test; Holt--Klee is a unit vertex-capacity maximum flow on every
face. For (a) and (b) we exhibit, for each class, a dyadic readout system of
order $(3,r)$ with $r=1$ for the Holt--Klee classes and $r=2$ for the other
two, found by successive linear programming and by a $(1+\lambda)$
evolution strategy in readout space, and then
\emph{verified in exact rational arithmetic}: $\val_\sigma$ on $\Vmax$ is the
componentwise minimum over \emph{all} piece selections, the outmap and
nondegeneracy are read off from it, and, by \Cref{thm:mono-iff}(b), the
explicit stopping SSG is built and re-verified from the game --- the trap
characterisation for stopping, then $T_\sigma(\text{cand})=\text{cand}$ at
every vertex, which identifies $\val_\sigma$ because a stopping game's operator
has a unique fixed point. For (c), $\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}$ is computed by
breadth-first search over unions of the agreement masks of all $656$
Holt--Klee AUSOs of the $3$-cube.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:mono-m3}
Part (b) is the negative half of \Cref{rem:blowup-realise}'s dichotomy
answered, at $m=3$, in the negative: there is \emph{no} structural obstruction
to be had. Every acyclic unique sink orientation of the $3$-cube --- including
the two that no linear programme over a cube can produce --- is presented by a
stopping game. In particular a game can present, on one face of its Max cube,
an orientation unrelated to the one it presents on the parallel face; the
``anti-value'' argument of \Cref{rem:blowup-realise} is not an obstruction but
a statement about one particular substitution. What is left of the negative
side is arithmetic: \emph{how many} Min vertices, and how large a game, a
prescribed orientation costs. \Cref{thm:mono-kbound} is the only lower bound of
that kind we can prove, and on the instances at hand it says only $k\ge1$.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Coverage at $m=4$]\label{rem:mono-cover4}
Sampling readout systems at random and reading off the orientation samples
exactly the realisable ones, and each hit is a realisation. With affine
readouts ($r=1$), $150000$ samples hit $541$ of the $12640$ classes of the
$4$-cube --- and \emph{every} hit is Holt--Klee: none of the $331+2273+3003+
832+87+1=6527$ non-Holt--Klee classes was hit, as \Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}
requires, while $215$ of the $423$ Holt--Klee classes of height $2$, $298$ of
the $2503$ of height $3$ and $27$ of the $2401$ of height $4$ were. With two
pieces per readout ($r=2$: one Min vertex per readout, twelve in all after
\Cref{thm:mono-iff}(b)) another $150000$ samples hit $434$ classes, and now
$44$ of them are \emph{not} Holt--Klee --- $32$ of the $331$ non-Holt--Klee
classes of height $2$ and $12$ of the $2273$ of height $3$. So a single Min
vertex per readout already buys, at $m=4$, forty-four orientations that no
one-player game and no linear programme over a cube can produce. Random
sampling reaches only low heights, so its silence above height $4$ is not
evidence; this is the same warning as \Cref{rem:mono-gap}.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[$G^{\sharp}$ as a readout system]\label{prop:mono-gsharp}
The game $G^{\sharp}$ of \Cref{prop:auso-seven} has, computed exactly from the
game, eight readouts $\Psi_{v,a}$ each a minimum of at most \emph{two} distinct
substochastic affine maps of the other three Max values (five of the eight are
single affine maps); the outmap recomputed from those eight functions alone is
the height-$7$ orientation
$(0,1,3,6,7,4,13,10,14,15,9,12,11,8,5,2)$. So the height-$7$ orbit is realised
by a readout system of order $(4,2)$, and three Min vertices suffice for it in
the construction of \Cref{thm:mono-iff}(b) --- one for each non-affine readout.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A computation in exact rational arithmetic from the explicit game: expand the
average part (a DAG) to the harmonic normal form over the controlled vertices,
eliminate the two Min vertices for each of the four $\tau$ to get affine maps
over the four Max values, and solve away each vertex's own value as in
\Cref{lem:mono-reduce}. The fixed point of each selection is computed by exact
elimination, $\val_\sigma$ as the componentwise minimum over all $4^{4}$
selections; the fixed-point identity and nondegeneracy are asserted at each of
the $64$ incidences.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The translated face is realised, already by one player}

\begin{definition}[Carrying a translate]\label{def:mono-translate}
Let $F$ be a face of the $m$-cube of dimension $d+1$, $c$ a free coordinate of
$F$ and $j\ne c$ another. Say $s$ \emph{carries a single-coordinate translate
at inner dimension $d$} if for some such $F,c,j$ the two $d$-faces
$F\cap\{x_c=0\}$ and $F\cap\{x_c=1\}$, read as outmaps of the $d$-cube on the
free coordinates other than $c$, satisfy
$s|_{x_c=1}(v)=s|_{x_c=0}(v\oplus e_j)$ and are not equal. When $F$ is the whole
cube ($d=m-1$) call it a \emph{facet} translate. This is exactly the operation
$B$ of \Cref{thm:blowup} performs between its layer $(0,0)$ and its layer
$(1,0)$, with the vector $z$ that \Cref{rem:blowup-measured} shows is a single
coordinate from the second level on.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The operation is not the obstacle]\label{prop:mono-translate}
Of the $728$ acyclic unique sink orientations of the $3$-cube, $168$ --- four
classes --- carry a facet translate (inner dimension two):
\[
 \begin{array}{lcll}
 (0,1,2,3,5,4,7,6) & h=2 & \text{Holt--Klee} & (c,j)=(2,0)\\
 (0,1,3,2,7,6,4,5) & h=3 & \text{Holt--Klee} & (c,j)=(1,0),(2,1)\\
 (0,1,3,2,5,4,6,7) & h=2 & \text{not Holt--Klee} & (c,j)=(1,0),(2,0)\\
 (0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4) & h=3 & \text{not Holt--Klee} & (c,j)=(1,0)
 \end{array}
\]
By \Cref{prop:mono-m3} all four are improvement orientations of stopping SSGs,
and the first two are improvement orientations of \emph{one-player} stopping
SSGs, whose readouts are single substochastic affine maps. In the first, the
facet $x_2=0$ carries $(0,1,2,3)$, whose sink is $v=0$, and the facet $x_2=1$
carries $(1,0,3,2)$, whose sink is $v=1$. Moreover the height-$7$ orientation
of \Cref{prop:auso-seven}, realised by the two-player $G^{\sharp}$, carries
four single-coordinate translates at inner dimension two (and twenty at inner
dimension one); $B^{2}$ carries three at inner dimension three --- its own,
between the layers $(0,0)$ and $(1,0)$ --- twenty-one at inner dimension two
and fifty-eight at inner dimension one.

At $m=4$, $182$ of the $12640$ classes carry a facet translate, i.e.\ a
single-coordinate translate of a \emph{$3$-cube}, which is the inner dimension
$B^{2}$ needs. Thirteen of them --- four of the four Holt--Klee classes of
height $2$, eight of the fourteen of height $3$ and one of the nineteen of
height $4$ --- are improvement orientations of nondegenerate \emph{one-player}
stopping SSGs, found by random readout sampling and verified exactly; the games
have $55\le N\le145$ vertices (four Max, no Min) and denominators $64$ to
$1024$. An example is the height-$4$ class with outmap
$(7,2,13,8,3,6,9,12,15,10,0,5,11,14,4,1)$ and translate pair $(c,j)=(0,2)$,
realised on $77$ vertices at denominator $128$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The $3$-cube enumeration is the one of \Cref{prop:mono-m3} and its
realisations are the exact witnesses produced there; the counts for the
height-$7$ orientation and for $B^{2}$ are a direct scan of all faces. At
$m=4$ the property is invariant under the automorphism group --- a translate
pair $(c,j)$ maps to $(\pi(c),\pi(j))$, and the condition is symmetric in the
two faces --- so it is tested on the $12640$ class representatives of
\Cref{prop:auso-size}'s census. The thirteen realisations come from sampling
affine readout systems at random ($250000$ samples) and reading off the
orientation, which samples exactly the one-player-realisable ones; each hit is
then rounded to a dyadic readout system and verified as in
\Cref{prop:mono-m3}, ending with a check from the explicit game.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:mono-translate}
\Cref{prop:mono-translate} settles the third ingredient of
\Cref{rem:blowup-realise} in the negative direction, and more sharply than
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured}'s realised $B$ of the $2$-cube does. There the
translation was by $\bar1$ and the game had four Max vertices; here the
translation is by a \emph{single coordinate} --- the case that occurs from the
second level of the blow-up on --- and the game can be a \emph{one-player}
game, so every readout is a single monotone affine map of the other Max
values. There is therefore no theorem of the form ``the values of an SSG
cannot present, on one face, the translate of what they present on the
parallel face''. The anti-value
$\val(j^{(0)})+\val(j^{(1)})-\val(j)$ of \Cref{rem:blowup-realise} is an
obstruction to one particular substitution, not to the operation: what a face
of the Max cube presents is the sign pattern of $\Psi_{v,1}-\Psi_{v,0}$ at
$2^{m-1}$ points, and those points move with the layer. The inner dimension is not the obstacle either: at $m=4$ thirteen
one-player games translate a whole $3$-cube between parallel facets, which is
what the second level of the blow-up asks for. What is not settled is the rest
of $B^{2}$'s structure --- two outer coordinates, the parity rule, and the
height that comes with them. \Cref{rem:mono-gap} states that gap.
\end{remark}

\subsection{How many pieces almost every orientation costs}

\begin{proposition}[Counting in readout space]\label{prop:mono-count}
The number of outmaps of the $m$-cube realised by readout systems of order
$(m,r)$ is at most $2^{O(rm^{3}\log(2r))}$, while the number of acyclic unique sink
orientations of the $m$-cube is at least $728^{2^{m-3}}>2^{1.18\cdot2^{m}}$.
Hence there is $c>0$ such that all but a $2^{-\Omega(2^{m})}$ fraction of the
acyclic unique sink orientations of the $m$-cube require more than
$c\,2^{m}/m^{4}$ affine pieces in some readout, and therefore, by
\Cref{thm:mono-iff}(a), more than $m-4\log_2 m-O(1)$ Min vertices --- and so
$2^{\Omega(m)}$ vertices --- in any realisation.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A readout system of order $(m,r)$ is a point of $\mathbb R^{n}$,
$n=2rm^{2}$. For each $\sigma$ and each selection of one piece per coordinate,
$x_\sigma$ is by Cramer's rule a ratio of determinants of size $m$ in those
coordinates, so each of the $m2^{m}$ conditions
$\Psi_{v,1-\sigma(v)}(x_{\sigma,-v})-x_\sigma(v)\gtrless0$ is, after clearing
positive denominators, the sign of a polynomial of degree $O(m)$ --- more
precisely the outmap is determined by the sign vector of the $O(r^{m}m2^{m})$
polynomials obtained by ranging over the selections as well, still of degree
$O(m)$. There are at most $M=r^{m}m2^{m}$ such polynomials (one local-optimality test
per selection, coordinate and $\sigma$, together with the $m2^m$ sign
conditions themselves). Warren's bound gives at most $(4eDM/n)^{n}$ sign
vectors for $M$ polynomials of degree $D$ in $n$ variables, here
$2^{O(rm^{2}(m\log r+m))}=2^{O(rm^{3}\log(2r))}$. For the lower bound,
if coordinate $i$ is \emph{combed} --- every $i$-edge oriented from the facet
$x_i=0$ to the facet $x_i=1$ --- and the two facets carry acyclic unique sink
orientations, the result is again one: the Szab\'o--Welzl condition across the
facets is witnessed by $i$ itself, and a cycle would have to stay in one facet.
So $A(m)\ge A(m-1)^{2}$ with $A(3)=728$, giving $A(m)\ge728^{2^{m-3}}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:mono-count}
This is \Cref{prop:auso-size} in the currency of \Cref{thm:mono-iff}, and the
counting half is that proposition's argument; what is added is that the bound
now falls on the number of \emph{Min vertices}, not only on the total size,
and that the lower bound $A(m)\ge728^{2^{m-3}}$ is proved here rather than
quoted. It also fixes the sense in which the negative side of
\Cref{rem:blowup-realise} is true: almost every acyclic unique sink
orientation is unrealisable at subexponential size. That says nothing about
$B^{2}$, which is not a random orientation, and \Cref{prop:mono-m3} shows
there is no obstruction of a purely combinatorial kind to be had.
\end{remark}

\subsection{What is missing}

\begin{remark}[The gap]\label{rem:mono-gap}
\Cref{prop:mono-m3} closes $m\le3$, \Cref{prop:mono-gsharp} adds a
four-dimensional non-Holt--Klee witness and \Cref{prop:mono-translate} realises
the translate operation itself, but the general question is open in one
sentence: \emph{is every acyclic unique sink orientation of the $m$-cube
realised by some readout system of finite order, equivalently by some stopping
SSG with $m$ Max vertices?} \Cref{prop:mono-count} says the answer must be no
for almost all of them once ``finite order'' is read as ``polynomial order'',
so the sharp question is which ones, and the sharp missing statement for the
pivot is: \emph{is $B^{2}$ --- the $5$-cube orientation
$(7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6,24,9,27,14,31,28,29,10,16,25,19,30,23,20,21,26,8,17,11,22,15,12,13,18)$
of bottom-antipodal height $10$ --- realised by a readout system of order
$(5,r)$ for some small $r$?} The nearest thing we can prove about it is
\Cref{thm:mono-kbound}, and it is weak: six of its forty $3$-faces have
$\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}=2$ and the other thirty-four have $1$; seven of its ten
$4$-faces are not Holt--Klee, but every one of the ten has
$\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}\le2$ (a branch-and-bound over the acyclic unique sink
orientations of the $4$-cube agreeing with the face on at least eight of the
sixteen vertices, of which a two-part cover must contain one, together with a
search for a Holt--Klee completion on the complement). So all we get is
$k\ge1$: any realisation of $B^{2}$ needs at least one Min vertex. The same
computation gives $\chi_{\mathrm{HK}}=2$ for the height-$7$ orientation at
$m=4$, where $G^{\sharp}$ uses two Min vertices, so the bound is not tight
there either.

Two warnings about what a negative answer would buy. First, excluding $B^{2}$
would not bound any all-switches run: a bound on $f$ needs a height bound for
\emph{every} realisable orientation, and \Cref{prop:auso-size} already forbids
obtaining that by enumeration; \Cref{prop:mono-count} shows the same in the
readout parametrisation. Second, our searches must not be read as evidence.
Successive linear programming in readout space, with a trust region and
restarts, reached at best $52$ of the $64$ incidences of the height-$7$
orientation at $m=4$ in $38$ restarts with $r=2$, $32$ with $r=3$ and $22$ with
$r=4$ --- and \Cref{prop:mono-gsharp} shows that orientation \emph{is} realised
with $r=2$. The same method reached $126$ of $160$ incidences of $B^{2}$. A
failed search in this space proves nothing at all.
\end{remark}
